name: Iharkutosuchus
sum: Small Late Cretaceous eusuchian from Hungary with multicusped, mammal-like teeth, probably a plant eater.
wsnote: Estimated body length about 80 cm, with a skull up to 11.1 cm long.
holotype: MTM 2006.52.1, a nearly complete skull — Csehbánya Formation, Iharkút, Bakony Mountains, Hungary (Ősi et al. 2007).
material: Several other partial skulls, isolated skull bones and numerous teeth.
biology: Strongly heterodont, with some teeth complex and multicusped like those of mammals. The skull structure allowed grinding with a mobile lower jaw, supported by extensive horizontal wear facets, and together with the teeth points to a diet of fibrous plant material. Its enamel shows a pattern convergent with mammalian Hunter-Schreger bands.
author: Osi et al. 2007
